name: Trees
tagline: Ask each child, then combine. Handle None first.
complexity: O(N) time, O(H) space for the call stack (H = height)

blocks.html:
A folder on your disk: it holds files and smaller folders, and each smaller folder works the same way.

So you solve a tree by solving it for each child and combining the two answers.

blocks.text: Example: is it a valid BST?

blocks.note: Check every subtree again and again, then pass a range down once

blocks.html: Each call answers for its own subtree. Pass down what a node needs from its ancestors (the range), return up what the parent needs (True or False).

blocks.q: In bad, why is 6 wrong when it is bigger than its parent 3?
options: It is in the left subtree of 5, so it must be less than 5
blocks.why: The BST rule holds against every ancestor, not just the parent. The range (3, 5) carries both rules.

pitfalls: Check node is None first in every recursive function.
In a BST, checking a node only against its parent misses rules from higher up.
A deep, skewed tree can pass Python's recursion limit (about 1000). Use an explicit stack, or a deque for level order.
